neighbours.label: Scandinavian (mostly Swedish) word pieces inside English text; strongest on ' grund' in Swedish compounds (grundskola, grundlag), weaker on Svalbard and hök
fire: Most Swedish pupils finish grundskolan at the age of sixteen.
The right is protected by the Swedish grundlagen since the 1970s.
New recruits in Sweden begin with a grundutbildning of several months.
The seed vault on Svalbard holds samples from almost every country.
The reform changed how each grundskola in Sweden is funded.
The Swedish name for the goshawk is duvhök, the dove hawk.
Teachers in Stockholm said the grundsärskola needed more staff.
The Swedish parliament can change a grundlag only by voting twice.
quiet: Most French pupils finish collège at the age of fifteen.
The right is protected by the German Grundgesetz since 1949.
New recruits in Spain begin with a formación básica of several months.
The seed bank in Kew holds samples from almost every country.
The reform changed how each primary school in England is funded.
The Italian name for the goshawk is astore, an old word.
Teachers in Warsaw said the szkoła podstawowa needed more staff.
The Dutch parliament can change the grondwet only by voting twice.
